summary: Zorya Nikolayevna Petrunicheva was an Indologist who graduated in history from Moscow State University around 1943–1948. In 1953, she served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Zsigmond Telegdi specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the Budapest University of Jewish Studies, Eötvös Loránd University (PhD, PD), and under Émile Benveniste, later serving as Professor of General Linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1958–1979).

Zsuzsanna Renner works in Indology and history/archaeology, having earned an MA from Eötvös Loránd University (1978–1986). In 2017, she was an Honorary Associate Professor at Eötvös Loránd University and a Senior Research Fellow at the Archaeolingua Foundation.

Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Teacher Training College, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna. She served as a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University and the Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016).

Zuicho Tachibana worked in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied as a disciple under Kozui Otani around 1903–1914 and under Edward Denison Ross around 1910–1912.

Zuiei Ito was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, earning doctorates from both. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1980 to 2013.
Zuigan Goto was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the Second Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and under Sokatsu Shaku. He served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

Zuiho Yamaguchi specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and EPHE under Jacques Bacot and Rolf Alfred Stein, later serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1970–1986) and Nagoya University (1986).

Zuiryu Nakamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Kenryu Tsukinowa and Susumu Yamaguchi. In 1945, he became a professor in the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University.

Zygmunt Rysiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv and under Jerzy Kuryłowicz, Louis Renou, Theodor Bloch, and Émile Benveniste. In 1949, he taught comparative linguistics at the University of Warsaw.
Gyurme tubten nyinje studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pad+ma la studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ármin Vámbéry worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. In 1865, he became Professor of Oriental Languages at Eötvös Loránd University, and he also held a post at Nyugat.

Ènver Ahmedovič Makaev was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University and Moscow State Linguistic University. He taught at Moscow State University (1938–1960) and served as a professor at the RAS Institute of Linguistics (1954–1976).
Édouard Biot was a Sinologist who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and Stanislas Julien.

Édouard Chavannes was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure, Collège de France, and INALCO under Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys, he served as a professor at the Collège de France (1893–1918).

Édouard Huber was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes, among others. He was director at EFEO (1901–1905) and Professor of Indochinese philology at the Sorbonne (1912–1914).
Édouard Lancereau was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions as a professeur suppléant at Lycée Charlemagne and as a correcteur at the Imprimerie Nationale.
Édouard Specht was a Sinologist who studied under Jean-Pierre-Guillaume Pauthier and Stanislas Julien. In 1892, he taught Chinese at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Édouard-Simon Ariel was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf from 1840 to 1844. In 1846, he became Conservator at the Bibliothèque publique de Pondichéry.
